title: Computing hydration free energies and crystalline solubility of drug-like molecules with MACE
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33408v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate prediction of thermodynamic solubility is critical in drug discovery, where it influences oral bioavailability and drives decisions in formulation chemistry. First-principles calculations of intrinsic solubility offer the potential to achieve superior generalization to existing direct, data-driven predictors, which often suffer significant performance degradation outside of their training distribution. Whilst free energy perturbation calculations provide a rigorous framework to estimate these quantities, their accuracy is typically limited by the quality of the empirical force field used. In this work, we present a computational workflow driven by the MACE family of machine learning interatomic potentials to compute the solubility of neutral drug-like molecules. We introduce $\lambda$-MACE, a potential optimised for condensed-phase free energy calculations, which enables hydration free energy calculations at experimental accuracy on an evaluation set of 70 compounds from the FreeSolv database selected for their relevance to medicinal chemistry. We further combine these hydration free energy calculations with sublimation free energy calculations to predict crystalline solubility given a known experimental crystal structure, on an additional set of 10 compounds. We achieve state-of-the-art performance for each leg of the calculation, with experimental accuracy for the hydration leg, and accuracy competitive with industry-standard DFT for the sublimation leg. However, the overall errors after combining both legs lead to accuracy of 1.53 log units. This is significantly above the experimental accuracy (0.17-0.6 log units). Closing this gap will require substantially tighter accuracy in each leg, on the order of half of chemical accuracy (0.5 kcal/mol), with crystalline thermodynamics the hardest remaining challenge.
relevance_reason: Key author: G\'abor Cs\'anyi

title: A general-purpose electron density model for molecular chemistry
abstract:
arXiv:2611.34732v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Universal machine-learning potentials predict molecular structure and stability at the accuracy of quantum mechanics, for a fraction of the cost. Properties derived instead from knowledge of the electronic structure give profound insights into chemical reactivity, but are not accessible with the same ease or transferability. We train PET-rho-OMol25, a model of the ground-state electron density and spin polarization of molecular systems on four million OMol25 structures in multiple charge and spin states. The model makes predictions for entire proteins in a few seconds on a single GPU, and enables estimation of important diagnostics of molecular structure and reactivity, such as vibrational Stark measurements, halogen $\sigma$-holes, hydrogen-bond basicities and core-level shifts, as well as spin density for redox chemistry and magnetism. PET-rho-OMol25 has an accuracy close to density-functional theory, with its least reliable predictions flagged by its built-in uncertainty estimator, for most properties and classes of compounds. It can be used as a drop-in replacement for electronic-structure calculations of the density, making insightful analyses available for larger and more complex structures.
relevance_reason: Key author: Michele Ceriotti

title: High-Throughput Orientation Extraction via Symmetry-Adapted Filters
abstract:
arXiv:2611.34541v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An algorithm for finding the orientation of objects in an image that have a known rotational symmetry, the symmetry-adapted filter (SAF) algorithm, is presented. It is deterministic and training-free, which makes it fast and reproducible. A filter that encodes the known rotational symmetry and approximate peak width is centered on the symmetry center of the object of interest, masked to the region of interest, and rotated to maximize its inner product with the image. The approach is demonstrated on more than 20,000 small-angle neutron scattering images of a torque-driven skyrmion lattice. It is also demonstrated on atomically resolved real-space images, where mapping local atomic orientations enabled the identification of grains and grain boundaries and the quantification of lattice relaxation.
relevance_reason: Key author: Tess Smidt

title: EGQCA Code: automated high-throughput thermodynamic modeling of solid solutions
abstract:
arXiv:2611.34551v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modeling disordered systems from first principles across the full composition range is a long-standing computational challenge. We present a code package implementing the extended generalized quasichemical approximation (EGQCA), which describes solid solutions through the statistics of a finite set of clusters and enables their thermodynamic modeling at arbitrary compositions and temperatures. The package automates the complete workflow and interfaces with both DFT codes and universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs). We show that replacing DFT with uMLIPs reduces the cost of the cluster calculations by up to five orders of magnitude while preserving the thermodynamic predictions. To make computationally demanding properties tractable, we additionally introduce a cluster-selection algorithm that identifies the most relevant configurations. Together, these developments establish EGQCA as a fast and accurate framework for the thermodynamic modeling of solid solutions and a practical route toward high-throughput screening of disordered materials.
relevance_reason: Key author: Chris Pickard

title: Guidance as Variance Matching
abstract:
arXiv:2611.34801v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Guidance repels the prediction of a diffusion model away from a weaker reference prediction. It substantially improves sample quality, but its mechanism remains poorly understood. We first find that, at the scales used in practice, guidance does not improve the prediction of the posterior mean (the model's training target); it makes the prediction worse, while samples improve. Second, posterior-mean predictions have less variance than the data, and we find that guidance restores it. We introduce variance-matched guidance: a closed-form rule that picks the guidance scale by matching the variance of the guided predictions to that of the data. Without tuning, it recovers the hand-picked scales of eleven widely used models across image, video, audio, motion, and world generation; to our knowledge, no previous explanation of guidance predicts them. Applied per noise level, it yields a schedule without tuned hyperparameters that users prefer to hand-crafted ones on SD 3.5 Medium. Third, we offer an interpretation of the mechanism behind guidance: each model makes a random error in predicting the posterior mean, and guidance rescales the difference of these errors into a sample with the posterior's covariance, which improves sampling. This view also suggests two new hypotheses that our experiments support: guidance can work with negative scales, and guiding a model with its own checkpoint needs a larger scale than guiding it with an independently trained model.
relevance_reason: Key author: Tommi Jaakkola

title: ILMlip: fast and universal machine-learning interatomic potentials
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33538v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large-scale pretrained machine-learned interatomic potentials keep growing more accurate as new models appear at a rapid pace, and more expensive: the current leader of Matbench Discovery as of November 2026 (F1 score 0.935) has $9.9\times10^7$ parameters and took 3.6 thousand GPU-hours to train. The ILMlip potentials presented here are optimised for speed as well as zero-shot accuracy. They are equivariant, conservative message-passing potentials in which every component is arranged for throughput: little work per pair of atoms and as much as needed per atom. Through ASE on one GPU, they run molecular dynamics up to about $10^3$ times faster than state-of-the-art message-passing potentials such as MACE (medium) and up to five times faster than NEP89 and DPA-4.1C. At the same time, six sizes with $1.4\times10^5$ to $2.8\times10^7$ parameters, pretrained on materials, molecules and solid acids, reach F1 scores of 0.75 to 0.91 on Matbench Discovery, placing the largest within 0.03 of the current leader. They therefore suit high-throughput, large or long simulations, and, being transferable, they are strong starting points for fine-tuning. Fine-tuned to six materials, the model of size S comes close to the ab initio force errors of a fine-tuned MACE, so it reaches reference-level accuracy at about 50 ns per atom and step (Cu fcc). Their components can be adopted separately, as a starting point for architectures with even better ratios of speed to accuracy. The ILMlip implementation is available at https://github.com/jhaens/ilmlip
relevance_reason: Presents new equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials with training, benchmarking, and MD speed/accuracy tests, clearly satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Foundation interatomic potentials capture structural disorder in metallic glasses
abstract:
arXiv:2611.34156v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials transfer well across chemical and structural space, yet their reliability for highly disordered metallic states is less established. Metallic glasses are a demanding benchmark: they have traditionally been modeled with Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potentials fitted to specific compositions, while ab initio molecular dynamics remains too expensive at the required sizes and timescales. Using the prototypical Cu-Zr-Al glass, we show that foundation potentials capture structural disorder, reproducing the structure, quenching dynamics, and elastic, mechanical and thermal properties of the amorphous state at near first-principles accuracy. We benchmark MACE foundation models against a classical EAM potential along molecular dynamics quenches, validating against density functional theory and experiment, first at Cu46Zr46Al8 and then across the good glass-forming region of the ternary. We further test two specialization routes: fine-tuning on glass structures generated with Lennard-Jones surrogate models, and on automatically generated small periodic cells (ASSYST). Models pre-trained on databases that include non-equilibrium liquid and amorphous configurations, such as OMAT, are accurate and transferable across composition out of the box, clearly outperforming the composition-specific EAM potential. Fine-tuning on target glass structures brings only modest gains, while specialization on small crystalline cells degrades the description of disorder. The readiness of foundation potentials for disordered metals is therefore set mainly by the diversity of their pre-training data rather than by system-specific fine-tuning, shifting the modeling effort from bespoke dataset generation to pre-training coverage and careful validation of the resulting dynamics.
relevance_reason: Benchmarks MACE foundation MLIPs against EAM and DFT along MD quenches for Cu-Zr-Al metallic glasses, directly developing/testing an MLIP-driven simulation workflow, satisfying (a), (b) and (c) fully.

title: Anisotropic Crystallization Kinetics and Interfacial Dynamics of Phase-Change Material Sb$_2$S$_3$
abstract:
arXiv:2605.20785v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Antimony sulfide (Sb$_2$S$_3$), an Earth-abundant and sustainable chalcogenide, has emerged as a promising phase change material (PCM) due to its ultra-low optical losses, broadband transparency, and reversible phase-change capacity. In this work, we developed a machine learning force field based on the moment tensor potential approach, allowing us to understand the atomistic origin of the structural evolution and crystallization kinetics in Sb$_2$S$_3$ for the first time, by enabling large-scale molecular dynamics simulations (up to 7680 atoms for 40 ns). Sb$_2$S$_3$ has anisotropic growth rates with the (100) facet ($Pnma$ space group) exhibiting the fastest growth due to the strong Sb-S covalent bonding along its quasi-1D ribbon-like structure of its crystalline phase. The maximum growth rate was observed at 875 K, with an optimal undercooling degree of ~100 K, significantly lower than other PCMs like Ge$_2$Sb$_2$Te$_5$ (GST) and GeTe. The activation energy for crystal growth was calculated be around 0.56 eV. Interfacial atomic dynamics revealed an Arrhenius-to-non-Arrhenius transition at ~800 K, with the (100) facet showing the highest diffusion activation energy of 1.56 eV. Unlike the GST and GeTe, the lower activation energy for crystal growth in Sb$_2$S$_3$ indicates that its heterogeneous crystallization is interface-controlled rather than diffusion-limited, with atomic attachment at the solid-liquid interface being energetically favoured over long-range atomic transport. Bonding and ring statistics analyses confirmed that directional covalent bonding plays a fundamental role in guiding structural ordering during crystal growth. These findings provide key insights into the structural, thermodynamic, and kinetic properties of Sb$_2$S$_3$, paving the way for optimizing its functionality including switching speed, reliability, and energy efficiency.
relevance_reason: Develops a moment-tensor machine-learned force field and runs large-scale MD on explicit Sb2S3 atomic systems, satisfying (a), (b), and (c).

title: OrbACE: Orbital and Atomic Cluster Expansion
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33743v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate electronic-structure reference data are expensive, motivating interatomic potentials that learn effectively from limited training sets. We introduce OrbACE (Orbital and Atomic Cluster Expansion), a framework that supplements an E(3)-equivariant cluster-expansion backbone with inexpensive electronic-structure descriptors. On ANI-1x at the $\omega$B97X/6-31G* level, its atom-centered variant, OrbACE-A, trained on 10,000 configurations and evaluated on 442,000 held-out configurations, achieves energy and force mean absolute errors of 3.16 meV/atom and 76 meV/angstrom in direct learning, compared with 9.61 meV/atom and 146 meV/angstrom for MACE with matched backbone settings. This reduces the energy error by a factor of three and approximately halves the force error. Its energy error is also below that of the best delta-corrected MACE baseline, 5.00 meV/atom, although its force error is slightly higher. Combining OrbACE-A with a Hartree-Fock delta baseline further reduces the errors to 1.48 meV/atom and 35 meV/angstrom.
  OrbACE-A builds atom- and pair-resolved invariants from a non-self-consistent extended-Hueckel model evaluated within the differentiable forward pass, yielding forces consistent with the predicted energy. The orbital variant, OrbACE-O, instead uses localized Hartree-Fock orbitals as graph nodes, with scalar and equivariant electronic descriptors. Its forces are evaluated at fixed descriptors, omitting their response to nuclear motion. In direct learning on ANI-1x, its energy error is approximately three times that of OrbACE-A. The three benchmarks considered (ANI-1x, revised MD17, and 3BPA) cover neutral, closed-shell, non-periodic molecules containing H, C, N, and O. Performance outside this domain remains to be established.
relevance_reason: OrbACE develops and benchmarks an MLIP with orbital/electronic descriptors for energies and forces; (a) explicit atomic configurations, (b) MLIP development/training/benchmarking, and (c) advances MLIP methodology.

title: Origin of the anomalous shape of the $\gamma$-loop in paramagnetic Fe1-xCrx alloys from coupled Atomistic Spin Dynamics and ab initio Molecular Dynamics
abstract:
arXiv:2611.34565v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The region of fcc stability in Fe-rich Fe-Cr alloys, the $\gamma$-loop, has an anomalous shape: at low temperatures, Cr addition initially stabilizes fcc, but above 8 at.% Cr it stabilizes bcc. At high temperatures, Cr always stabilizes bcc. This behavior reflects a delicate balance between magnetic, vibrational and configurational free-energy contributions that is challenging to capture from first principles. We investigate phase stability in Fe1-xCrx (x = 0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15) using coupled atomistic spin dynamics and ab initio molecular dynamics with thermodynamic integration. Gibbs free energy differences between fcc and bcc are calculated from 800 to 1800 K. Our calculations reproduce the experimental $\gamma$-loop and its compositional dependence, with near-quantitative accuracy for the $\gamma$-$\delta$ transition. The $\alpha$-$\gamma$ boundary, including its anomalous shape, is reproduced qualitatively, although transition temperatures are underestimated by approximately 200 K. Static calculations of magnetically ordered and disordered states provide an explanation: in ordered states, increasing Cr initially reduces the energetic preference for bcc over fcc, whereas in disordered states, Cr progressively stabilizes bcc at all compositions. Vibrational effects contribute to phase stability, while atomic short-range clustering at higher Cr content ($x \geq 0.15$) may explain the observed closing of the $\gamma$-loop from below. The simulations reveal finite Cr moments in the paramagnetic state, whose magnitudes depend on their local magnetic environment. The results demonstrate that the anomalous $\gamma$-loop arises from the interplay of magnetic energetics, magnetic disorder, lattice vibrations and chemical clustering, which must be treated on equal footing to capture phase stability from first principle
relevance_reason: Couples atomistic spin dynamics with ab initio molecular dynamics and thermodynamic integration to compute fcc/bcc free energies in Fe-Cr alloys, clearly satisfying (a), (b) and (c) with enhanced/free-energy sampling on explicit atoms.

title: Exascale Multi-Task Graph Foundation Models for Imbalanced, Multi-Fidelity Atomistic Data
abstract:
arXiv:2604.15380v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We present an exascale workflow for atomistic graph foundation models using HydraGNN. Multi-task learning enables joint training across 16 heterogeneous first-principles datasets representing over 467 million unique structures (over 544 million cumulative branch records) and covering 85+ elements. A shared graph neural network backbone with dataset-specific prediction heads accommodates the strongly imbalanced, multi-source, multi-fidelity corpus, supported by scalable ADIOS2/DDStore data management. Composition-conditioned weighting combines source-specific predictions into a single deployable model. Six large-scale hyperparameter optimization campaigns, followed by resource-aware continual training on 2,048 Frontier nodes, identify PaiNN as the lead architecture under a fixed computational budget. We evaluate scalability across Frontier, Aurora, and Perlmutter and characterize transfer across twelve down-stream tasks, including comparisons with pretrained UMA and MACE models under different adaptation strategies. These results reveal task-dependent transfer benefits and highlight the importance of matching adaptation strategies to downstream applications. Finally, we assess inference optimizations and BF16/FP32/FP64 precision tradeoffs, achieving the screening of 1.1 billion atomistic structures in approximately 50 seconds on Frontier. Together, these results establish a scalable framework for multi-source atomistic foundation model training, evaluation, and high-throughput deployment, thereby allowing for a fast and reliable exploration of vast chemical design spaces that are otherwise inaccessible to first-principles methods
relevance_reason: Develops and benchmarks atomistic graph foundation models / ML interatomic potentials such as PaiNN, UMA, and MACE on explicit structures, satisfying (a), (b), and (c).

title: SCO-Hyper-Meta-Double-GroupNN: A Double-Group SU(2) Hyper-/Meta-Graph Neural Network for Cooperative Spin-Crossover Potential Energy Surfaces
abstract:
arXiv:2611.34547v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Learning potential energy surfaces for magnetic materials requires resolving coupled local spin manifolds and geometric frustration. We introduce SCO-Hyper-Meta-Double-GroupNN, a geometry-only architecture combining a pretrained O(3)-equivariant backbone with SU(2) spinor Hamiltonians and cooperative hyper-/meta-graph interactions. Analytic thermal spinor density matrices provide non-polynomial two- and three-body structural invariants, while frustrated-triangle hyperedges and a multi-shell sideway gate couple geometric representations to local spin manifolds. A variationally consistent, doubly-centered zero-gauge free-energy functional couples multiplet occupations and signed spin orientations, yielding conservative autograd forces without spin inputs at inference. On a first-principles Co-Cr-Ni benchmark comprising 346 training and 59 held-out validation supercells across crystalline, amorphous, glassy, and liquid regimes, compact models with 56k-77k parameters outperform a 207k-parameter spin-conditioned magnetic MACE baseline. Energy MAE decreases by 37-44%, reaching 3.82 versus 6.83 meV/atom, and force MAE decreases by 10.8-14.2 meV/Angstrom, reaching 165.8-169.2 versus 180.0 meV/Angstrom. The models preserve Kramers degeneracy to within $6\times10^{-15}$ eV, predict equilibrium local magnetic moments from geometry alone with an absolute-moment MAE of $0.181\,\mu_B$, and support stable molecular dynamics up to 2,200 K. This framework integrates local spinor symmetry and cooperative magnetic interactions into geometry-only interatomic potentials.
relevance_reason: Development and benchmarking of a geometry-only equivariant machine-learned interatomic potential (with SU(2) spinor Hamiltonians) trained on first-principles Co-Cr-Ni supercells, validated by energy/force MAE against a MACE baseline and stable MD to 2200 K, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: gREST-ABMD: A general enhanced-sampling framework for free-energy calculations across QM/MM, coarse-grained, and all-atom models
abstract: To explore the free-energy landscapes of biomolecules using molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, various enhanced sampling methods have been developed. One representative approach is to use a few collective variables (CVs), while the other is to enhance global motions of a whole system or a part of it under extreme conditions, such as high temperatures or high pressures. The former is implemented using biasing potentials, and the latter often uses replica-exchange algorithms. Here, we integrate these two approaches by developing a new method called generalized replica exchange with solute tempering-adaptively biased molecular dynamics (gREST-ABMD). In this method, ABMD, which uses time-dependent biasing potentials along CVs, is integrated with the gREST method. In addition to gREST-ABMD, we implemented ABMD variants, including multiple-walker ABMD (MW-ABMD), replica-exchange ABMD (RE-ABMD), and bias-exchange ABMD (BE-ABMD), within the GENESIS software. These algorithms are now available in MD simulations using multi-scale models, including quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM), all-atom, and coarse-grained (CG) models. We tested these algorithms in simulations of three systems: the proton-transfer reaction in malonaldehyde using QM/MM, the conformational change of adenylate kinase using CG, and the folding of chignolin using all-atom models. In all the cases, the free-energy landscapes and other physical properties converged quickly. They were in good agreement with those obtained with other enhanced sampling methods while using much fewer computational resources.
relevance_reason: Develops and implements gREST-ABMD enhanced-sampling free-energy methods with replica exchange and adaptive biasing validated in QM/MM, coarse-grained, and all-atom MD simulations, clearly satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Geometry Sets the Neutral MLIP-DFT Gap in Non-Covalent Binding, and Charged Systems Fail
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33830v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are widely expected to substitute for explicit quantum chemistry when screening molecular interactions. On non-covalent binding we find that this expectation holds for neutral chemistry and fails for charged chemistry. We audit the FAIRChem UMA OMol head, without task-specific fine-tuning, on 5,567 probe-target dimers from 18 benchmarks across nine fidelity arms, using RAPIDS (Rapid Atomistic Probe-target Interaction Discovery Scaffold), a training-free inference-time scaffold. First, on neutral chemistry RAPIDS reaches a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.37 kcal/mol, matching or beating every explicit DFT single-point fidelity (1.42-1.50 kcal/mol), so the remaining MLIP-DFT gap is geometric rather than a learned-surface error. Second, charged systems form a qualitatively different regime: MAE jumps to 8.5-22.9 kcal/mol across three charged benchmarks; DFT single-point rescoring does not restore accuracy, geometry reoptimization restores it for ionic hydrogen bonds and ion-molecule dimers, and the failure persists across all three MLIP backbones. Third, the residual failures are structured: signed biases cluster by chemistry family, and whether a fidelity fails catastrophically transfers across families more reliably than error magnitude, enabling cost-aware fidelity selection. RAPIDS-Select, a closed-form rule on cheap precomputed features, uses about 37% less compute than a strong static DFT baseline at matched accuracy, and on a newly computed charged benchmark cuts the catastrophe rate from 68% to 5.7%. On WetSenseBench, a wet-lab-grounded host-guest selectivity benchmark from eight sensing studies, RAPIDS without DFT follow-up recovers 82.9% pair-level agreement on the seven studies above its ~1 kcal/mol precision floor.
relevance_reason: Audits universal MLIP-DFT binding accuracy on explicit dimers with geometry reoptimization; (a) explicit atomic geometries, (b) MLIP benchmarking and geometry optimization, and (c) applies/benchmarks MLIPs for non-covalent interactions.

title: Stability and superstructural ordering of alkali-triel-pnictide clathrates A$_8$T$_{27}$Pn$_{19}$
abstract:
arXiv:2604.05264v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Clathrates are a class of inclusion compounds that offer various useful and surprising phenomena, including superconductivity, thermoelectricity, and the potential for high-density ion storage. Stability conditions within the Alkali-Triel-Pnictide A$_8$T$_{27}$Pn$_{19}$ family of unconventional clathrates are investigated with high-throughput density functional theory calculations, establishing trends in formation energy, structural and electronic properties, and identifying several new potential candidates. Electronic structure calculations and first-principles molecular dynamics simulations show that all alkali guests are fully ionized in the framework, and that the stability of electron-exact clathrates correlates with the ionization potential of the guest atoms, while their rattling behavior is governed primarily by the size of the guest ions relative to the cages. Targeted reactive synthesis from elemental precursors is attempted, resulting in four previously unreported ternary phases, two of which are structurally characterized. However, the predicted clathrate phases are not obtained. Further analysis reveals that the stability of ATPn clathrate compounds containing heavy elements, such as bismuth, depends strongly on relativistic spin-orbit coupling, which is often neglected in high-throughput studies that compute formation energies. Finally, chemically induced superstructural ordering is described in relation to Wyckoff sites in the prototypical type-I clathrate unit cell.
relevance_reason: Uses high-throughput DFT and first-principles molecular dynamics on explicit clathrate atomic structures, satisfying (a), (b), and (c) for atomistic stability and structural/electronic-property analysis.

title: Predicted high-$T_{\rm c}$ superconductivity above 130 K in metastable cubic MH$_4$ compounds at ambient pressure
abstract:
arXiv:2511.04222v2 Announce Type: replace-cross 
Abstract: Hydrides have long been considered promising candidates for achieving room-temperature superconductivity; however, the extremely high pressures typically required for high critical temperatures remain a major challenge in experiment. Here, we use high-throughput first-principles calculations to propose a class of high-$T_{\rm c}$ ambient-pressure superconductors with MH4 stoichiometry. These hydrogen-based compounds adopt the bcc PtHg4 structure type, in which hydrogen atoms occupy the one-quarter body-diagonal sites of metal lattices, with the metal atoms acting as chemical templates for hydrogen assembly. Through comprehensive first-principles calculations, we identify three promising superconductors, PtH4, AuH4 and PdH4, with superconducting critical temperatures of 84 K, 89 K, and 133 K, respectively, all surpassing the liquid-nitrogen temperature threshold of 77 K. The remarkable superconducting properties originate from strong electron-phonon coupling associated with hydrogen vibrations, which in turn arise from phonon softening in the mid-frequency range. Moreover, ab initio molecular dynamics simulations demonstrate that PtH4 remains kinetic stable at 300 K over 20 ps, with no atomic diffusion observed.
relevance_reason: High-throughput DFT (electron-phonon coupling, phonons) on explicit MH4 crystal structures plus ab initio molecular dynamics at 300 K to test kinetic stability, so (a) explicit atoms, (b) DFT/AIMD, and (c) materials application are all satisfied.

title: Effects of Yttrium doping on Proton Conductivity in Ba(Fe, Co, Zr, Y)O$_{3-\delta}$ Cathode Materials for Proton Ceramic Fuel Cells
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33543v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Protonic ceramic fuel cells (PCFCs) offer efficient energy conversion at intermediate temperatures, but their performance is often constrained by sluggish oxygen reduction kinetics at the cathode. Triple conducting perovskite materials such as BaCo$_x$Fe$_y$Zr$_z$Y$_{1-x-y-z}$O$_{3-\delta}$ (BCFZY) have shown promise as air electrodes. In this study, we investigated the impact of Y doping on proton conductivity by decoupling the effects on proton diffusivity and proton concentration. Using ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) simulations, we assessed proton tracer diffusivity across three compositions: BaCo$_{0.4}$Fe$_{0.4}$Zr$_{0.2}$O$_{3-\delta}$ (BCFZ), BaCo$_{0.4}$Fe$_{0.4}$Zr$_{0.1}$Y$_{0.1}$O$_{3-\delta}$ (BCFZY0.1) and BaCo$_{0.4}$Fe$_{0.4}$Y$_{0.2}$O$_{3-\delta}$ (BCFY). Thermodynamic defect models incorporating hydration, oxidation, and hydride formation reactions are employed to estimate temperature-dependent proton concentrations. Our results suggest that increasing the Y content from BCFZ to BCFY increases proton diffusivity by 1.7% at 500 $^\circ$C. Under PCFC operating gas conditions, proton concentration and proton conductivity are predicted to increase by 3.8% and 5.3%, respectively, at 500 $^\circ$C. These increases are modest compared with the larger enhancements reported experimentally under reducing conditions, highlighting the importance of gas conditions in evaluating the effects of Y doping. Under low oxygen partial pressure conditions, we predict that the dominant proton transport mechanism shifts from hydroxyl groups (OH$_O^{\bullet}$) to hydride species (H$_O^{\bullet}$). This work provides mechanistic insight into proton transport in BCFZY cathodes and offers design principles for optimizing proton-conducting air electrodes in next-generation PCFCs.
relevance_reason: Runs ab initio molecular dynamics simulations of proton diffusion in doped perovskite cathodes, satisfying (a)-(c) with explicit atoms and AIMD application.

title: Solvent-Mediated Disintegration of a Vitrimer Network
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33770v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Vitrimers are dynamic polymer networks characterized by associative bond exchange, which enables topological rearrangement while preserving the overall network connectivity. However, how this dynamic connectivity evolves in the presence of a solvent, particularly as a function of temperature, remains poorly understood. Here, we employ hybrid molecular dynamics Monte Carlo simulations to elucidate the temperature-dependent restructuring and dissociation of vitrimer networks in solution. By constructing temperature composition phase diagrams, we demonstrate that the critical temperature for network dissolution increases nonlinearly with crosslink concentration. We find that the network disintegration begins well below the critical dissolution temperature, indicating that the loss of network connectivity can occur even before the onset of macroscopic dissolution. However, the network undergoes extensive restructuring around the critical temperature for a highly crosslinked system, resulting in the formation of numerous smaller, disconnected networks. Concurrently, the number of intrachain dynamic bonds increases with temperature. Interestingly, complete disintegration into individual polymer chains is not observed; instead, the solution comprises a broad distribution of smaller network fragments. These findings reveal the complex interplay between solvent-induced network disintegration and dynamic bond redistribution, providing molecular level insights into the dissolution of vitrimer networks and their potential for solvent assisted recycling.
relevance_reason: Uses hybrid molecular dynamics Monte Carlo simulations to study vitrimer network disintegration, satisfying (a)-(c) with explicit atomistic MD/MC.

title: Computational Study of Water Adsorption and Dissociative Mechanisms Impacting g-C3N4's Optical and Electronic Properties
abstract:
arXiv:2607.26667v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: In the quest for sustainable energy solutions, water splitting emerges as a crucial process for generating clean hydrogen a versatile and renewable fuel essential for energy storage, emissions reduction, and achieving sustainability goals. This study employs a comprehensive computational approach, utilizing atomistic simulations to systematically investigate the effects of water absorption on the electronic and optical properties of g-C3N4 nanosheets. Our methodology integrates ab initio computations grounded in density functional theory (DFT), which allows for a detailed characterization of the nanosheet and serves as a benchmark for self-consistent charge density functional tight binding (SCC-DFTB) simulations. This approach provides valuable insights into the behavior of the nanosheet under the influence of absorbed OH and H2O molecules by considering calculated parameters for photocatalytic efficiency. Additionally, we extend our investigation to classical molecular dynamics simulations within the ReaxFF framework, modeling the emission of multiple H2O molecules and assessing the subsequent rate of H2 evolution. A key finding of our study reveals that the dissociation of H2O into HO and O molecules significantly enhances both the optical absorbance and conductance of the nanosheet compared to its pristine state. These results underscore the potential of g-C3N4 nanosheets as effective materials for water splitting applications.
relevance_reason: Combines DFT, SCC-DFTB, and ReaxFF molecular dynamics on explicit g-C3N4/water atomic systems, satisfying (a), (b), and (c).

title: Adaptive alchemical continuation for resource-efficient absolute binding free-energy prediction
relevance_reason: Title presents adaptive alchemical continuation for absolute binding free-energy prediction, which is an atomistic free-energy simulation methodology, satisfying (a)-(c).

title: Analytic sc$GW$ nuclear gradients with the resolution-of-identity approximation
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33536v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present the first fully analytic derivation and implementation of nuclear gradients for the finite-temperature sc$GW$ method. The derivation is formulated within the $\Phi$-derivable framework of sc$GW$, using a Lagrangian formulation to obtain the analytic gradients. With the resolution-of-identity approximation, the computational cost of evaluating the gradients scales as $O(N_{\tau}N_\text{aux}^{2}N_\text{AO}^{2})$, exhibiting the same asymptotic scaling as the parent sc$GW$ method. Using the newly implemented analytic gradients, we perform geometry optimizations for several molecular systems and benchmark the resulting structures against those obtained with Hartree--Fock, $G_{0}W_{0}$, MP2, CCSD, and CCSD(T). We find that sc$GW$ generally yields reasonable molecular geometries, with its performance being comparable to that of CCSD for several systems. Overall, these results demonstrate the potential of analytic sc$GW$ gradients for reliable geometry optimizations for molecular systems while retaining the favorable $O(N_{\tau}N_\text{aux}^{2}N_\text{AO}^2)$ scaling of the underlying method.
relevance_reason: Analytic scGW nuclear gradients enable geometry optimizations of molecular systems; (a) explicit atoms, (b) GW/post-HF method development plus geometry optimization, and (c) advances electronic-structure and structure-optimization methodology.

title: On the binding and stability of CeO2 molecules on low-index Au surfaces
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33338v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Many multi-phase thin films grown by self-assembly involve co-deposition of both metallic and oxide phases that grow into the same film. Under such conditions, the oxide species may be present in stoichiometric molecular form on the surface of the metallic phase. Quantifying the stability, binding, and diffusion of such molecular oxide states on metallic surfaces is critical for understanding self-assembly. In this work, we investigate the binding and stability of CeO2 molecules on Au surfaces using spin-polarized density functional theory calculations. Specifically, we examine how the configuration of the CeO2 molecule, its binding energy and binding free energy, structural stability, effective charge, and projected electronic density of states vary among various binding sites on Au(001), Au(110), and Au(111) surfaces. Molecular CeO2 was found to be more favorable on all Au surfaces than its atomic constituents. It was also found that the bent CeO2 molecule configuration is more stable than the linear counterpart, with the Ce atom on the hollow site and the O atoms on the top sites. In addition, the configurations of the CeO2 molecule on Au surfaces with a binding energy around or weaker than -1 eV were found to have a low probability of existence above room temperature. Furthermore, the charge transfer was found to occur in such a way that the CeO2 molecule becomes polarized on all surfaces, but the polarization is stronger only for the strongly bonded states on Au(001) and Au(110) surfaces. Finally, three different cases of how the CeO2 molecule binds to Au(001), Au(110), and Au(111) were identified: case 1: chemisorption with symmetric bonds, case 2: chemisorption with asymmetric bonds, and case 3: physisorption with symmetric bonds. These three cases of CeO2 binding are present on Au(001) and Au(110), but only cases 2 and 3 occur on Au(111).
relevance_reason: Uses spin-polarized DFT to study CeO2 binding, stability, free energy, and diffusion on Au surfaces; (a) explicit surface/molecule atoms, (b) DFT calculations, and (c) applies DFT to a real material system.

title: Bringing Singles to $GW$: A Coupled-Cluster Perspective on Orbital Relaxation
abstract:
arXiv:2611.34160v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The one-shot $G_0W_0$ approximation suffers from a pronounced dependence on the underlying mean-field starting point. Here, we explore an alternative to conventional self-consistent $GW$ schemes by introducing single excitations within the recently established connection between $GW$ and extended coupled-cluster (ECC) theory. Starting from the equivalence between $G_0W_0$ and ionization-potential/electron-affinity equation-of-motion direct-ring extended coupled-cluster doubles (IP/EA-EOM-drECCD), we extend the formalism to include right-hand single-excitation and left-hand single-deexcitation cluster amplitudes coupled to the direct-ring doubles amplitudes. The resulting approximation, denoted singles-$G_0W_0$ (s$G_0W_0$), incorporates orbital-relaxation effects without explicitly introducing self-consistency in the Green's function. We assess the performance of s$G_0W_0$ for molecular valence and core ionization potentials using Hartree-Fock and Kohn-Sham starting points. For both types of ionizations, the inclusion of singles largely suppresses the starting-point dependence observed in conventional $G_0W_0$, yielding quasiparticle energies close to those obtained from the Hartree-Fock reference, irrespective of the initial mean-field description. Although this does not necessarily translate into improved absolute accuracy, it demonstrates that singles provide an effective route to reducing the starting-point dependence of $GW$-like approximations without resorting to self-consistency.
relevance_reason: Introduces singles into GW via an extended coupled-cluster perspective for molecular ionization potentials; (a) explicit molecular atoms, (b) GW/CC electronic-structure method development, and (c) advances post-HF/many-body methodology.

title: Exact subtraction of electron self-interaction from the Kohn-Sham equations
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33795v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The self-interaction error (SIE) of Kohn-Sham density functional theory (KS-DFT) leads to a non-physical, non-linear dependence of an orbital's energy on its own fractional occupation [Dabo et al., Phys. Rev. B, 82:115121, 2010]. The generalized Koopmans condition (GKC) ensures an atomic orbital's eigenenergy is independent of its fractional occupation$-$ and is free of self-interaction. The constrained search of the Levy spin-density-functional theory yields orbital densities and delivers the ground-state energy to generalize the Hohenberg-Kohn theorems. In this work, the electron density of the Kohn-Sham equations is constrained to be orbital-density dependent, with a total energy functional linear with respect to variation of its orbital densities. That is, the KS multiplicative effective potential $v_{\text{s}}[{n}]$ for an orbital $\varphi_i[{n}]$ is constrained to a functional $v_{\text{eff}}[{n - n_i}]$. The result complies with the generalized Koopmans condition (GKC). This approach improves LDA and GGA mean absolute errors (MAEs) in fundamental band gaps by $\sim$ 1 eV, with respect to KS-DFT. Equations free of electron self-interaction provide the basis for improvements in the accuracy, efficiency, and simplicity of density functional theories.
relevance_reason: Develops a Kohn-Sham DFT correction for electron self-interaction, satisfying (a)-(c) as a DFT method advance on explicit electronic/atomic systems.

title: Multiscale Numerical Modelling of Ultrafast Laser-Matter Interactions: Maxwell Two Temperature Model Molecular Dynamics (M-TTM-MD)
abstract:
arXiv:2601.20763v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: In this work, we present a comprehensive numerical framework that couples numerical solutions of Maxwell's equations using the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) approach, Molecular Dynamics (MD), and the Two-Temperature Model (TTM) to describe ultrafast laser-matter interactions in metallic systems at the atomic scale. The proposed Maxwell-Two-Temperature Model-Molecular Dynamics (M-TTM-MD) bridges the gap between electromagnetic field propagation, electron-phonon energy exchange, and atomic motion, allowing for a self-consistent treatment of energy absorption, transport, and structural response within a unified simulation environment. The calculated electromagnetic fields incorporate dispersive dielectric properties derived using the Auxiliary Differential Equation (ADE) technique, while the electronic and lattice subsystems are dynamically coupled through spatially and temporally resolved energy exchange terms. The changes in the material topography are then reflected in the updated grid for the FDTD scheme. The developed M-TTM-MD model provides a self-consistent numerical framework that offers insights into laser-induced phenomena in metals, including energy transport and surface dynamics under extreme nonequilibrium conditions.
relevance_reason: The paper develops a coupled Maxwell-TTM molecular dynamics framework for laser-metal interactions with explicit atomic motion, satisfying (a)-(c) as a classical MD method/application.

title: Efficient all-electron Bethe-Salpeter implementation using crystal symmetries
abstract:
arXiv:2603.24860v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We describe an all-electron implementation of the Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) for the calculation of optical absorption spectra in the full-potential linearized augmented-plane-wave (FLAPW) method. So far, FLAPW implementations have resorted to a simple plane-wave basis for the bare and screened Coulomb potentials, thereby forgoing the all-electron description to some extent. In contrast, we expand the interaction potentials in the all-electron mixed basis. As in most implementations, the BSE is solved by the diagonalization of a two-particle Hamiltonian matrix, whose dimension is proportional to the number of $\mathbf{k}$ points. Because of the large number of $\mathbf{k}$ points required to converge the BSE, the resulting matrix becomes large even for small unit cells. We describe a method that exploits the crystal symmetries to accelerate the construction and diagonalization of the two-particle Hamiltonian. In particular, we employ group theoretical tools to bring the Hamiltonian into block-diagonal form. Furthermore, it is shown that often only one of the blocks needs to be taken into account for the optical absorption spectrum, leading to a considerable speedup of the diagonalization step. The code allows for the inclusion of spin-orbit coupling and is parallelized with the possibility of storing the Hamiltonian in distributed memory over many nodes, keeping the memory demands low. To validate our implementation, we show optical absorption spectra and report exciton binding energies for bulk Si, LiF, and MoS$_2$. By exploiting the crystal symmetries, we can reduce the dimension of the Hamiltonian matrix of Si by a factor of five, resulting in a 125-fold speedup in its diagonalization. The calculated exciton binding energies of 22~meV and 76~meV for Si and MoS$_2$ are closer to experimental values than in previous BSE studies.
relevance_reason: The paper implements an all-electron FLAPW Bethe-Salpeter equation method exploiting crystal symmetries for optical spectra, satisfying (a)-(c) as a post-DFT electronic-structure method development on explicit atomistic crystals.

title: Dressed Time-Dependent Density Functional Theory: Opening and Closing a Pandora's box
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33377v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Dressed time-dependent density functional theory (DTDDFT) has been shown to overcome the inability of adiabatic TDDFT to describe excitation energies and oscillator strengths of double-excitation character, however, it is far from being a black-box method. Here, we outline and address several operational issues while benchmarking the approach on a range of molecules. We define a protocol to determine whether an excitation from adiabatic TDDFT needs a double-excitation correction, without requiring a priori knowledge of the state, and which Kohn-Sham states to build the frequency-dependent DTDDFT matrix from. We present an 'undownfolding' that replaces this frequency-dependent matrix by a linear frequency-independent one in a larger space, eliminating ambiguities in the iterative procedure required to diagonalize the former. We compare the performance of DTDDFT for both excitation energies and oscillator strengths, as measured by an approximate metric for their single-excitation character, for different choices of the underlying adiabatic density functional approximation, with and without employing the Tamm-Dancoff approximation, for molecular excitations predicted by wavefunction methods to have either partial or genuine double-excitation character. We propose a correction to DTDDFT to account for missing dynamical correlation that is removed in the truncation procedure inherent in the method, and discuss the possibility of unphysical imaginary frequencies reminiscent of the 'triplet instability' that may arise. We provide benchmark data for butadiene, hexatriene, octatetraene, cyclopentadiene, acrolein, naphthalene, ethylene, borole, and cyclopentadienone. In some cases, DTDDFT predicts frequencies with about as much accuracy as the same underlying adiabatic TDDFT predicts for the constituent and near-lying single excitations.
relevance_reason: Method development for dressed TDDFT excitation energies and oscillator strengths in molecules; (a) explicit molecular electronic structure, (b) DFT/TDDFT method development, and (c) advances an electronic-structure method, though it involves no dynamics.

title: Electron--phonon interactions in a pseudo--atomic orbital basis: superconductivity, transport, spectroscopy and thermal emission from one interpolated vertex
abstract:
arXiv:2611.33473v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Electron--phonon interactions govern superconductivity, electrical resistivity, optical absorption and electronic excitation lifetimes in solids. First--principles calculations require interpolating this coupling onto dense Brillouin--zone grids, traditionally using maximally localized Wannier functions that demand material--specific tuning. Here we show that a fixed basis of pseudo--atomic orbitals--automatically generated from pseudopotentials and implemented in the open--source code PAOFLOW captures the electron--phonon vertex with equivalent accuracy and no manual tuning. Computed from density--functional perturbation theory or displaced supercells, and incorporating long--range fields and spin--orbit coupling, the vertex matches established codes on identical inputs. We validate the method on lead, reproducing its phonon dispersion, superconducting gap, critical temperature, resistivity, photoemission kink and cyclotron masses, and on silicon, capturing phonon--assisted optical absorption, wafer emissivity and carrier mobilities. This parameter--free framework enables high--throughput, automated electron--phonon calculations across large materials databases.
relevance_reason: Develops a DFT/DFPT-based electron-phonon interpolation method using pseudo-atomic orbitals and explicit atoms, satisfying (a)-(c) as a first-principles method advance, though it is not MD.

title: Magnetic Contributions to Phase Stability in the Co-Ni Binary: A First-Principles CALPHAD Study
abstract:
arXiv:2607.12388v2 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: We propose a simple method to employ ab-initio calculations to determine magnetic contributions to free energy of alloys. Validation on the Co-Ni binary demonstrates that this ab initio approach reproduces experimental FCC-HCP phase equilibria while providing physically transparent, structure-dependent magnetic parameters suitable for multicomponent extrapolation. Our results demonstrate that physically grounded magnetic parametrization, derived directly from electronic structure calculations, enables predictive phase diagram modeling for magnetic alloy systems.
relevance_reason: Uses ab initio electronic-structure calculations on explicit alloy structures to derive magnetic free-energy contributions for Co-Ni phase stability, satisfying (a), (b), and (c) as a DFT-driven CALPHAD application.

title: Uphill Diffusion in Yukawa Plasmas
abstract:
arXiv:2611.34459v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: In a fluid mixture of many species an individual species can diffuse toward higher concentration without any external driving force because its flux is coupled to the gradients of other components. Such `uphill diffusion' is well known in the chemical and metallurgy literature but to our knowledge has not been studied for strongly coupled plasmas in neutron star and white dwarf interiors. We have previously developed a semi-analytic diffusion model that accurately predicts diffusion coefficients of individual species in a mixture in equilibrium. Uphill diffusion allows us to test this model out of equilibrium, and also test a generalized Darken relation for predicting diffusivities. We derive an analytic theory and compare to three-component molecular dynamics simulations and find very good agreement. This provides a novel out-of-equilibrium test of the generalization of our diffusion model to arbitrary multi-component mixtures.
relevance_reason: The authors perform classical molecular dynamics of explicit Yukawa plasma particles and compare diffusion coefficients to theory, satisfying (a) explicit particles, (b) MD, and (c) application to multicomponent transport.
